scene.summary: A Hungarian flatbed truck driver parks his truck, only to hear groaning coming from the open cargo bed. Investigating, he discovers an unseen victim lying on the flatbed who explains that the truck ran him over with both legs broken, and he has been lying there since last Tuesday, surviving only because he had been carrying two large bags of groceries. After a brief reaction of utter disbelief, the driver's absurdly nonchalant response is not to call an ambulance, but to toss the injured man a blanket because the nights are getting chilly. The humor comes from the dark, dry absurdity of someone living unnoticed on a truck bed for over a week, combined with the driver's casual profanity and completely inappropriate, practical caretaking.

characters.name: truck driver
characters.description: Middle-aged Hungarian tradesman/driver with dark receding hair, sideburns, stubble, wearing a utility vest over a collared shirt. He speaks in vulgar, aggressive colloquial Hungarian filled with coarse profanities ('bazme', 'mi a faszom', 'mi a gecit') and careless pragmatism.

characters.name: injured man on the flatbed
characters.description: Unseen man lying injured on the flatbed of the truck, heard only through speech bubbles and groans ('HRAHGHHRRR....', 'AAAARRRGH....'). He speaks plainly and matter-of-factly about his horrific ordeal.

panels.description: The truck driver steps out of the cab of his small flatbed truck and clicks his remote key fob ('RITY!') to lock it, with a sound effect on the windshield ('HLOTT!'). A sign painted on the side of the truck's cargo bed reads 'ÉTTŐ'IPAI KITTELEZÉS • 06'.
The driver stands behind the truck with his hands on his hips, startled by a loud groan ('HRAHGHHRRR....') emanating from the back of the truck, swearing in surprise.

The driver angrily confronts whoever is on the flatbed. An unseen victim explains from the flatbed that the truck hit him on Gubacs Teréz street and broke both his legs, and he has been lying there hurting ever since.
Leaning against the tailgate, the driver objects that he wasn't anywhere near there today; the injured man replies that the accident actually happened last Tuesday.
The driver scoffs, asking how the man hasn't starved to death over a week; the victim explains he had just come out of the grocery store with two big shopping bags when he got hit.
The driver puts a hand to his forehead, cursing in disbelief ('A KURVA ÉLET!') as he walks away toward the cab.
The back of the empty truck stands still while another agonized groan ('AAAARRRGH....') rises from the bed.
The driver returns and casually tosses a folded blanket ('pléd') onto the flatbed, telling the victim that nights are turning cold.

notes: 'ÉTTŐ'IPAI KITTELEZÉS' in r0 is a mangled, misspelled tradesman sign for 'Építőipari kivitelezés' (construction contracting), typical of Napirajz's phonetic and garbled background mock-signs.

The phone number painted on the tailgate across panels p1 to p7 (r3, r7, r11, r14, r16, r20, r22) reads '7722 • 683/FELVESZEM' ('.../I'LL PICK UP'), parodying Hungarian informal tradesman mobile listings where availability or extensions are humorously noted.
'Bazme' (in r4, r8, r21) is a common truncated dialectal/slang form of 'baszd meg' ('fuck it / fuck you / damn it'), used as a constant conversational filler.
'Mi a faszom?' in r2 literally means 'What the fuck/my dick?', expressing startled annoyance.
'Mi a gecit keresel a platómon...?' in r4 uses 'a gecit' (literally 'the spunk/cum') as an intensifier equivalent to 'what the fuck are you doing on my flatbed'.
'Fáj. Fájogat.' in r5 uses the frequentative/diminutive verb form 'fájogat' ('it aches a bit / throbs on and off'), adding a comically understated tone to having two broken legs.
'Gubacs Teréz út' in r5 is a humorous mashup parodying Budapest street names (blending Gubacsi út and Teréz körút/Terézváros).
'Ne kamuzzá!' in r12 is slang for 'Don't bullshit me!' / 'Quit lying!', with a dropped final imperative consonant ('kamuzzál' -> 'kamuzzá').
'A kurva élet!' in r15 literally means 'The whore life!', a very standard Hungarian profanity expressing exasperation or disbelief (similar to 'Holy fucking shit!').

The punchline in r21 hinges on absurd Hungarian domestic practicality: instead of calling an ambulance or rushing the man to the hospital after learning he's been trapped with broken legs on the flatbed for over a week, the driver simply throws him a fleece blanket ('pléd') because autumn nights are getting chilly.
